do_not_assume: That a default connector exists for every campus.
That a public opportunity is discoverable.
That completion creates the intended membership without verification.
goal: A bounded connection type and opportunity are ready for controlled staff testing.
steps: Define the real lifecycle, responsible team, completion condition, and escalation path.
Create or select the connection type.
Configure only the statuses that represent genuine lifecycle stages.
Choose whether sequential status mode matches the process.
Configure states, activities, sources, due-date rules, enabled views, and request security.
Create the opportunity with public summary and details.
Configure campus scope, connector groups, default connectors, placement groups, roles, member statuses, transfer controls, and workflows.
Create test requests through each intended intake path.
Exercise assignment, status movement, activity logging, future follow-up, transfer, placement, and completion.
Train connectors on the enabled v19 views before broad rollout.
title: Recipe: Configure a new connection pipeline

do_not_assume: That every red metric represents the same urgency.
That an empty visible list means the scoped queue is empty.
goal: Every selected request has a verified owner or an explicit disposition.
steps: Open the intended connection type and campus.
Filter to Active and Unassigned or Overdue requests.
Confirm due-date rules before prioritizing by lateness.
Group or sort by opportunity, campus, due date, or status.
Review connector capacity and eligibility.
Assign bounded batches to appropriate connectors.
Use Future Follow-up only when a real future date is known.
Transfer poor-fit requests instead of leaving them stalled.
Read bulk-action result counts and inspect exceptions.
Reopen the filtered queue and verify the remaining population.
Confirm the metric's campus, type, and opportunity scope.
Inspect the connection type's due-date calculation mode.
Check opportunity- and status-level due-date or due-soon offsets.
Confirm whether the request has a calculated due date.
Separate active requests from Future Follow-up, inactive, and completed requests.
Open a small sample of underlying requests and reproduce the expected calculation.
Stop when the discrepancy is explained or a version-specific defect is reproducible.
title: Recipe: Triage an unassigned or overdue queue

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: The request reaches the correct destination with ownership and placement preserved.
steps: Review current comments, attributes, activities, campus, connector, and due date.
Confirm transfer is preferable to completing or inactivating the request.
Search for the best destination opportunity.
Choose the destination campus and status when those controls are enabled.
Select the destination's default connector, current connector, another eligible connector, or no connector deliberately.
Set the destination due date and add a transfer note.
Verify the destination request details and activity history.
When ready for completion, verify final status, placement group, role, member status, requirements, and required completion note.
Complete the request.
Verify the resulting placement and inactive/completed state.
title: Recipe: Transfer and complete a request safely

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: An eligible audience enters a controlled, assignable follow-up queue.
steps: Create or select the destination connection type and opportunity.
Configure the connector group and campus rules.
Build and validate the audience Data View.
Configure family limits and an opt-out group.
Choose All at Once or As Needed based on workload and request-age semantics.
Configure daily assignment limits, recurrence, and previous-connector preference where appropriate.
Confirm connector membership and any per-connector overrides.
Run a small controlled campaign cycle.
Compare eligible people, campaign-list entries, created requests, assignments, and exclusions.
Verify connector visibility and completion handling before increasing scale.
title: Recipe: Launch a connection campaign

do_not_assume: That registration success proves person matching, check-in eligibility, or staff follow-up.
That the presence of relevant Rock tables proves the flow is configured.
goal: A preregistered family reaches a verified staff-owned next step without avoidable duplicate records.
steps: Explain the practical value of preregistration on the public page.
Collect only the information required for the arrival and follow-up process.
Test person and family matching with representative scenarios.
Verify check-in eligibility and campus handling.
Create the intended workflow or connection request using reviewed mappings.
Preserve only an appropriate source reference and approved attributes.
Verify the request's opportunity, status, campus, comments, and assignment.
Complete a staff follow-up test.
Inspect for duplicate or partial people and family records.
Repeat the full path before broad publication.
Confirm the request is in Future Follow-up state.
Inspect the stored follow-up date.
Confirm the date has passed in the installation's effective time context.
Inspect the Connection Request Workflow Triggers job's schedule and recent results.
Check whether another workflow or status rule changed the request after deferral.
Re-open the request without restrictive list filters.
Stop when the job, date, state, or filter condition explains the behavior.
title: Recipe: Connect preregistration to staff follow-up

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: A status rule moves only currently eligible requests and can be retried safely.
steps: Record the source status, destination status, Data View, job, and intended business rule.
Review the Data View with a bounded sample.
Confirm every returned request is still in the source status.
Remove unintended fixed cutoff dates or stale criteria.
If age in status matters, validate the available status-history evidence rather than assuming `ModifiedDateTime` represents the transition.
Run the automation through its configured job in a controlled scope.
Compare source and destination counts.
Verify request state consistency and review job history.
Re-evaluate the Data View to confirm moved requests no longer qualify.
Stop if history semantics or installed automation behavior cannot be verified.
title: Recipe: Validate status automation
